1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned Aga for the State, Shri Manish Yadav, learned
counsel for opposite party no.2 & 3 and perused the records.

2.  This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants with the prayer to quash impugned charge-sheet no. 457 of 2022 dated 19.09.2022 and cognizance order dated 01.11.2022 as well as entire proceedings of Case No. 4877 of 2022 (State Vs. Alok Gupta and others),
arising out of Case Crime No. 586 of 2021, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 406 and 377 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P.Act against applicant no.1, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 406, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants has submitted that opposite party no.3 is the wife of applicant no.1 and applicant nos. 2 to 4 are his family members.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants has further submitted that on account of matrimonial discord,
present criminal case has been instituted against the applicants by opposite party no.2, however subsequently, with the intervention of respected members of both the families, applicants and the opposite party no.2 & 3 have amicably and genuinely settled all their disputes and differences and now they do not have any grievance against each other.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicants has next drawn the attention of this Court to a compromise deed dated 29.05.2023, drawn between the parties, a copy of which has been annexed as Annexure-14 to his application.

6. Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that pursuant to the said compromise applicant no.1 has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- to opposite party no.3 in lieu of all her claims and dues and out of the same Rs.4,00,000/- has already been paid to her.
He has further submitted that the applicants have produced a demand draft no. 320628 for an amount of Rs.4,00,000/- in the name of opposite party no.3 which he has handed over to her today in Court.

It is further submitted that now nothing remains to be paid to opposite party no.3.
7.

Learned counsel for the applicants has next submitted that in view of the said compromise and in order to maintain harmonious and cordial relations between the parties, entire proceedings against the applicants be quashed.
8. Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 & 3 has also appeared and in paragraph 6 of the counter affidavit, he has acknowledged the said compromise.

He has further submitted that applicant no.1 has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- to opposite party no.3 in lieu of all her claims and dues out of which Rs.4,00,000/- has already been paid to her and further a draft of Rs.4,00,000/- in the name of opposite party no.2 has been received by her today in Court and now nothing remains to be paid to her.
In paragraph no.9 of the said counter affidavit, it has been categorically stated that opposite party no.2 and 3 have no objection, if the entire proceedings are quashed.
9. Learned AGA could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

10. This Court is not unmindful of the judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of:-
(1). B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another (2003) 4 SCC 675.
(2). Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation [2008) 9 SCC 677].

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.

13. Accordingly, the entire proceedings of Case No. 4877 of 2022 (State Vs. Alok Gupta and others),
arising out of Case Crime No. 586 of 2021, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 406 and 377 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P.Act against applicant no.1, under Sections 498-A, 323, 506, 406, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act against applicant no.2 and under Sections 498-A, 323, 506 and 406 IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act against applicant no. 3 and 4, Police Station Gandhi Park, District Aligarh, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate-Ist, Aligarh, are hereby quashed.
